column3: NASB renders “child” as “son.” A full-width colon appears in the NASB text.
NASB renders “Thankful I am” as “I thank,” “from my forefathers” as “the way my forefathers did,” and “pure” as “clear.”
NASB follows the critical text; it renders “having taken remembrance” as “I am mindful” and “I have been persuaded” as “I am sure.”
NASB renders “suffer together” as “join with me in suffering.”
NASB renders “given” as “granted” and “before eternal times” as “from all eternity.”
NASB follows the critical text without “of the Gentiles”; “herald” is rendered “preacher.”
NASB renders “my deposit” as “what I have entrusted to Him”; the phrase may also mean what He has entrusted to me, and the meaning is uncertain.
NASB follows the critical text; it renders “keep” as “Guard” and “the good deposit” as “the treasure which has been entrusted to you,” and reorders the verse.
NASB renders “You know this” as “You are aware of the fact.”
NASB follows the critical text; “household” is rendered “house,” and “chain” is “chains.”
NASB follows the critical text (“eagerly”); it ends the verse with a dash.
NASB sets the wish off with dashes and renders “how much he served” as “what services he rendered.”
